statuses.meaning: Executed successfully against an authorised lab target; command, output and environment recorded in audit/evidence.
Exercised with simulated output or fixtures — syntax and decision logic followed, but no real target was contacted.
Flags and quoting checked against the tool installed on the build host; no target was contacted.
Correct only where a specific tool, tool version or host configuration exists — the Prerequisites line names it.
Standard technique from the source handbook; not executed and not checked against an installed tool.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.privileges: user; root for -sS, -sU, -O and most NSE scripts
tools.compat: Checked on 7.99. --script names must exist in /usr/share/nmap/scripts.

tools.name: dig
tools.compat: AXFR only works if the server allows zone transfer.
usedBy: Directory & Virtual Host Enumeration — ffuf, Gobuster, Feroxbuster

tools.name: dnsenum
tools.compat: Wraps dig/WHOIS; the WHOIS stages need egress to the internet.

tools.name: dnsrecon
tools.compat: Flag names differ from dnsenum; --help is the reference.

tools.name: snmpwalk
tools.compat: Needs the community string; v1/v2c flags differ from v3 (-v 3 -l authPriv).

tools.name: onesixtyone
tools.compat: UDP only; does not traverse a SOCKS proxy.

tools.name: smtp-user-enum
tools.compat: VRFY/RCPT/EXPN support depends on the server; modern MTAs usually refuse all three.

tools.name: enum4linux-ng
tools.compat: The NG rewrite is Python 3 and takes different flags (-A instead of -a).

tools.name: showmount
tools.compat: -e lists exports; mounting needs root and the matching nfs kernel module.
usedBy: Linux Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: ldapsearch
tools.compat: AD answers LDAP on 389/636/3268; use -x for simple bind.

tools.name: smbclient
tools.compat: Checked on Samba 4.24.5. -N is an anonymous/null session, not a guest account.

tools.name: rpcclient
tools.compat: Legacy MS-RPC commands; many need credentials, a null session rarely answers them now.

tools.name: smbmap
tools.compat: Checked on 1.10.7. Empty -u/-p is a null session.

tools.name: NetExec
tools.privileges: user; admin on the target for Pwn3d!
tools.compat: Checked on 1.5.1. CrackMapExec (cme) is deprecated but still installs and takes the same arguments; prefer nxc.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam
Post-Exploitation & Lateral Movement — NetExec and Impacket
Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: Impacket
tools.install: sudo apt install python3-impacket  # or: pipx install impacket
tools.privileges: user; root for psexec, smbserver and ntlmrelayx (ports 445/80)
tools.compat: Kali and Debian install impacket-<module> wrappers; a source checkout or upstream pip install gives <module>.py. The arguments are identical.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam
Post-Exploitation & Lateral Movement — NetExec and Impacket
Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: BloodHound.py (collector)
tools.privileges: user with a valid domain credential
tools.compat: Needs DNS resolution of the domain and TCP to the DC. Writes a zip the BloodHound UI ingests.

tools.name: BloodHound (CE)
tools.compat: CE 7.x changed the default port and credentials from the 4.x generation; check the login screen before assuming neo4j/neo4j.

tools.name: Neo4j
tools.compat: BloodHound CE and 4.x expect different Neo4j versions; use the one BloodHound was packaged against.

tools.name: Certipy
tools.compat: The package is certipy-ad but the executable is certipy. Flags and output paths changed between v4 and v5 — run certipy -h. Not installed on the audit host.

tools.name: bloodyAD
tools.privileges: user with the relevant AD right
tools.compat: The command was renamed from bloodyAD.py to bloodyAD in 1.x. Not installed on the audit host.

tools.name: kerbrute
tools.package: release binary or go install github.com/ropnop/kerbrute@latest
tools.compat: Go binary, not a distro package on every build. User enumeration is loud in the DC logs.

tools.name: Hydra
tools.compat: Rate limits and account lockout are real; check the password policy before spraying.

tools.name: John the Ripper
tools.compat: Needs the jumbo build for --format=NT and most hash formats; the core build supports far less.

tools.name: ssh2john
tools.compat: Also shipped as ssh2john.py in /usr/share/john on some builds; output feeds john directly.

tools.name: hashcat
tools.compat: Rule files ship in hashcat-data and the set differs by release: best64.rule is absent on the audit host while other rules are present. Check ls /usr/share/hashcat/rules before using -r.

tools.name: hashid
tools.compat: Suggests candidates; it cannot tell two similar formats apart. Confirm with hashcat --example-hashes.

tools.name: curl
tools.compat: No default timeout: add --max-time on anything that can hang. -I is HEAD and behaves differently from a GET.
usedBy: Directory & Virtual Host Enumeration — ffuf, Gobuster, Feroxbuster
Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: wget
tools.compat: -m mirrors recursively; anonymous FTP needs anonymous:anonymous@ in the URL.
usedBy: Linux Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference
Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: WhatWeb
tools.compat: Checked on 0.6.4. -a sets aggression; default is passive.

tools.name: Nikto
tools.compat: Checked on 2.6.0. Very noisy; the exam rules may treat broad scanners as restricted.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.compat: Checked on 2.1.0-dev. -s hides connection errors and exits 0 with no hits, so do not use it blind.
usedBy: Directory & Virtual Host Enumeration — ffuf, Gobuster, Feroxbuster

tools.name: Gobuster
tools.compat: Checked on 3.8.2. dir and vhost share flags but not all of them.
usedBy: Directory & Virtual Host Enumeration — ffuf, Gobuster, Feroxbuster

tools.name: feroxbuster
tools.compat: Checked on 2.13.1. Recursive by default, which is noisier than ffuf.
usedBy: Directory & Virtual Host Enumeration — ffuf, Gobuster, Feroxbuster

tools.name: sslscan
tools.compat: Installed and checked here. Reports ciphers and protocol versions, not CVEs.

tools.name: testssl.sh
tools.install: sudo apt install testssl.sh  # or the upstream git checkout on $PATH
tools.compat: Not installed on the audit host. It is a shell script plus a bundled OpenSSL; --quiet suppresses the banner, not the findings.

tools.name: hakrawler
tools.compat: Not installed on the audit host and not packaged for Kali; -plain makes the output pipe-friendly.

tools.name: katana
tools.compat: Not installed on the audit host. ProjectDiscovery releases change flags often; -silent -d is stable.

tools.name: OpenSSL
tools.compat: Checked on 3.6.3. s_client needs </dev/null and -servername for SNI; without the redirect the pipe to x509 hangs.
usedBy: Linux Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: OpenSSH client
tools.compat: -o PreferredAuthentications=none is the fast way to list allowed methods.

tools.name: ssh-keygen
tools.compat: Legacy RSA/SHA-1 keys may be refused by newer servers; -m PEM helps old clients.

tools.name: scp
tools.compat: OpenSSH 9 defaults to the SFTP protocol; -O forces the legacy SCP protocol for old servers.
usedBy: Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: sshpass
tools.compat: Not installed on the audit host and not part of a minimal Debian install. For one known credential, not a wordlist loop.

tools.name: Evil-WinRM
tools.compat: Needs 5985/5986 and the account in Remote Management Users or Administrators.
usedBy: Post-Exploitation & Lateral Movement — NetExec and Impacket

tools.name: FreeRDP
tools.compat: Kali now ships the FreeRDP 3 binary; /cert:ignore and /dynamic-resolution replaced the old /sec:tls flags.

tools.name: netcat
tools.privileges: user; root to bind low ports
tools.compat: OpenBSD netcat has no -e; use mkfifo or the bash /dev/tcp trick. -w sets a timeout.
usedBy: Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference
Exploit Research & Payload Handling — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: socat
tools.privileges: user; root to bind low ports
tools.compat: The TCP4-LISTEN,reuseaddr,fork + EXEC:pty pair is what makes a shell stable.
usedBy: Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: chisel
tools.compat: The client must match the server version; run the binary for both sides.

tools.name: sshuttle
tools.privileges: root on the attacker host, SSH access to the pivot
tools.compat: Not installed on the audit host. Carries TCP only; UDP needs another tunnel.

tools.name: ProxyChains
tools.compat: TCP only. Check /etc/proxychains4.conf (not proxychains.conf on Kali) for the socks line.

tools.name: Python 3
tools.compat: python3 -m http.server is the transfer server; the pty module gives a stable shell.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam
Linux Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference
Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: msfvenom
tools.compat: Payload and encoder names change between releases (x64/x86 sha1 encoders are gone); msfvenom -l payloads is authoritative.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam
Exploit Research & Payload Handling — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: msfconsole
tools.compat: First start initialises the database and can take minutes. The exam rules restrict mass scanners and Metasploit modules — read them first.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam
Exploit Research & Payload Handling — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: searchsploit
tools.compat: Local copy of Exploit-DB; searchsploit -u updates it. Paths in old exploits are usually wrong for your target.
usedBy: Linux Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference
Exploit Research & Payload Handling — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: lftp
tools.compat: Not installed on the audit host. Optional: ftp and wget cover the same ground.

tools.name: ftp (client)
tools.compat: -p enables passive mode (not "port"). Interactive only, so it needs a TTY.

tools.name: ipmitool
tools.compat: Not installed on the audit host. Default credentials (ADMIN/ADMIN, root/calvin) are worth one attempt on IPMI 2.0.

tools.name: rlwrap
tools.compat: Gives history and line editing to shells and clients that have none; it is not a PTY fix on its own.
usedBy: Exploit Research & Payload Handling — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: mysql client
tools.compat: MariaDB and MySQL clients differ in some flags; --protocol=TCP forces the network path.

tools.name: noPac (PoC)
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/cube0x0/noPac && pip3 install -r noPac/requirements.txt
tools.compat: A PoC repository, not a package: run it from the clone directory. Not present on the audit host.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam

tools.name: PetitPotam
tools.compat: Ships as an example script inside Impacket; some packages install impacket-PetitPotam instead. Not present on the audit host.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam

tools.name: SharpHound
tools.install: copy from the BloodHound installation or the SharpHound release page
tools.compat: The .exe needs .NET; SharpHound.ps1 runs where execution policy allows. Output is a zip for the BloodHound UI.

tools.name: Rubeus
tools.install: download the release binary onto the target
tools.privileges: domain user; local admin for some actions
tools.compat: Defender flags the default build; rename or rebuild. Kerberos actions need a synced clock.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam

tools.name: mimikatz
tools.install: download the release binary onto the target
tools.compat: Almost always blocked by AV/Defender; lsadump::dcsync also needs DCSync rights or a DC.
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam

tools.name: PrintSpoofer
tools.install: download the release binary onto the target
tools.compat: Works on Windows 10/Server 2016-2019; patched behaviour on newer builds, where GodPotato or a different vector is needed.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: GodPotato
tools.install: download the release binary onto the target
tools.compat: Covers newer Windows builds where PrintSpoofer fails; still needs an impersonation privilege.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: winPEAS
tools.install: download the release binary onto the target
tools.compat: Very noisy and often flagged by AV; read the colour-coded output, do not paste it into a report.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: AccessChk (Sysinternals)
tools.privileges: user; -a on services is more reliable as admin
tools.compat: Accepts the EULA only with /accepteula on first run, which silently breaks scripted checks.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: certutil
tools.compat: Built in, but -urlcache -split -f is blocked or logged by some EDR products. It also hashes files (-hashfile).
usedBy: Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: net (Windows)
tools.privileges: user; admin for account and group changes
tools.compat: net user/group/localgroup are local; net rpc ... on Kali is Samba's client, a different tool with the same name.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: sc.exe
tools.compat: Quote the binPath value: sc create svc binPath= "cmd /c ..." needs the space after the equals sign.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: reg.exe
tools.compat: Use reg query/save/export; PowerShell's HKLM:\ paths are a different syntax and do not mix with reg.exe arguments.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: netsh
tools.compat: interface portproxy needs the IP Helper service running; rules survive reboots.

tools.name: schtasks
tools.compat: /ru SYSTEM requires an elevated shell; /tr quoting is the usual failure point.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: WMIC
tools.compat: Deprecated and absent on recent builds; PowerShell CIM cmdlets replace it.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: icacls
tools.privileges: owner or admin to change permissions
tools.compat: Grant syntax is /grant USER:(F) — the colon matters. Check with icacls <path> before and after.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: cmdkey
tools.compat: Stores credentials in the user profile; /list shows them, /delete:target removes them.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: msiexec
tools.compat: /q /i http://... pulls a remote MSI; /a is the administrative (extract) mode.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: klist
tools.compat: Shows the current logon session's tickets; purge with klist purge (not /purge).
usedBy: Bleeding Edge Vulnerabilities — NoPac, PrintNightmare & PetitPotam

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.compat: Execution policy and AMSI block many one-liners; -EncodedCommand is the usual workaround and is heavily logged.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: Get-Acl
tools.compat: Takes a registry or filesystem provider path: HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Vendor. A cmd.exe-style HKLM:SOFTWARE path is invalid.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: Get-FileHash
tools.compat: PowerShell only — it is not a cmd.exe built-in. certutil -hashfile is the cmd.exe equivalent.
usedBy: Shells & File Transfer — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: Invoke-PrivescCheck
tools.install: download PrivescCheck.ps1 onto the target and dot-source it
tools.compat: Dot-source the script first (. .\PrivescCheck.ps1) or the cmdlet is not found. -Extended is slower and much noisier.
usedBy: Windows Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.compat: Use -w to capture and read it back with -r; filtering on the interface you actually route through (tun0) avoids empty captures.

tools.name: linPEAS
tools.install: download linpeas.sh onto the target and chmod +x it
tools.compat: Architecture matters (amd64 vs arm64) and the script needs a shell plus read access. Very noisy output; the colour-coded HIGH/MEDIUM lines are what matter.
usedBy: Linux Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: pspy
tools.install: download pspy64 onto the target and chmod +x it
tools.compat: Watches process events without root; run it for several minutes to catch cron or timers.
usedBy: Linux Privilege Escalation — Complete Command Reference

tools.name: xsltproc
tools.compat: Transforms nmap XML into HTML with nmap's own .xsl from /usr/share/nmap/nmap.xsl.

tools.name: scrot
tools.compat: Needs DISPLAY (or Xvfb in a headless session). Proof screenshots must include the target IP in the same image.
usedBy: Exam Execution & Reporting — Proof, Timeline and Submission
